title: UI evidence and preview engine for plan reports

snapshot.basis: Read-only audit of workflow-axa and of the Cheflabels reference (D:\Cheflabels-labeler-V2) on 2026-11-03. Nothing was run, built or contacted.

understanding: Today a plan report shows the current screen as a screenshot when that is safe, and the proposed screen as a labelled sketch. You want real screens and real components wherever that is safe. Each element links to its real source and approval status. When an accurate picture is not possible, the report refuses visual approval.

boundaries: Only components explicitly marked approved count as approved. All others stay candidate or unverified (D4).
No application code changes in this task, and no invented UI to make a preview work. Anything a project needs is proposed to its owner as a separate task.
No invented HTML, CSS or SVG for application UI. D14 stays, and the report shell keeps the owner's design.
Visual approval is blocked when an accurate picture is impossible.
No production contact during capture. No installs except Playwright when a capture needs it, and each install is recorded (D2).
No screen that shows personal data is captured. No pixel blurring is promised.

screenshot_report.py captures local .html files only, at 1280 and 500 px, with no URL, element crop or ready wait. Proposed screens are always sketches.
evidence.limits: Read only. No capture was run.

evidence.claim: Before and after screens, arrows, hand-placed markers and decision callouts exist, up to six screens. Changes are not highlighted from the real page.
Reuse mode links an element to its source, tag, classes and wrapper, but not to a variant or an approval status. Decisions link to screens, not to elements.
No capture adapter or shared adapter interface exists. The Storybook reader is the only adapter-like code.
PNG structure and size limits are tested. Nothing records console errors, failed requests or missing assets for applications.
Presented reports are never overwritten. Reuse mode hashes only the files it cites, not every file a component depends on.
The offline report shell, its strict content policy, the owner's report design and the approval gates exist and stay.
Cheflabels has a real kit page at /design-kit with about 30 real components and fixed fixtures. Production builds remove it.
evidence.limits: Cheflabels files are outside this repository. This report cites them through FINDINGS only.

evidence.claim: Cheflabels keeps approval status only in the Status column of DESIGN.md. About 14 entries are not on the kit page.
The Cheflabels kit page still loads translations over HTTP, and the development environment points at the live backend. No offline translation folder exists.
evidence.limits: Cited through FINDINGS only. Nothing was contacted.

evidence.claim: Cheflabels has no Storybook and no Playwright. One earlier capture of the kit page exists.
Safe real Cheflabels screens need application changes: offline configuration, fixture translations, a fake session, user rights, data mocks and a browser that blocks non-local requests.
Live data screens, fresh translations, printing, the Wi-Fi wizard, camera, live updates and native safe areas cannot be captured without a server or device.
Altinstar (React 18, Vite 7) has Playwright 1.60 and a harness that renders real components with stubbed services. It injects its own styles and fonts.
Next.js needs mocks for server components and data. Vue on Vite is close to React. Unity has no DOM classes, so class mirroring does not apply.
Capture risks are production contact, committed tokens, personal data in images, running project code, and fidelity limits such as fonts and Ionic mode.

sections.title: Request
sections.text:
Show real screens and real components in plan reports wherever that can be done safely. Link every element to its real source and approval status. Refuse visual approval when an accurate picture is not possible.

This is a new, separate task from the owner's request of 2026-11-03.
sections.locator: PLAN.md ## Goal in plain words, ## Requirements

sections.title: What will change
sections.text:
Agreement r1 covers the requirements R1 to R10, the architecture, the boundaries and your answers D1 to D5. If a Cheflabels capture reaches the live backend, that preview stays blocked until a separate Cheflabels task makes it offline.

workflow-axa gets a framework-neutral evidence contract. Each capture has one manifest with the image, viewport, component and variant, approval status, decision IDs, runtime problems and dependency fingerprints. The renderer accepts a real preview only with a valid manifest.

Adapters behind one interface discover, render, capture, report runtime problems and fingerprint dependencies. The planned adapters are static HTML, Angular/Ionic for Cheflabels and React/Vite for Altinstar. Unity and other non-DOM screens use a manual capture, or visual approval is blocked.

Not included: application code changes, invented UI, production contact, pixel blurring and capture of screens with personal data. Playwright is the only install, and only when a capture needs it.

sections.title: How it will be built
sections.text:
Eight tickets, U-T1 to U-T8. U-T1 (manifest) and U-T2 (element verification) depend on nothing. U-T3 (adapter interface and static HTML adapter) and U-T4 (staleness) depend on U-T1. U-T5 (report view) depends on U-T1 and U-T2.

U-T6 (Cheflabels) and U-T7 (Altinstar) depend on U-T3. U-T6 captures the separate Cheflabels kit page (D3). If that page reaches the live backend, its previews stay blocked until a separate Cheflabels task makes it offline.

U-T8 depends on U-T6 if it is kept, on U-T7 and on U2.

sections.title: Decisions
sections.text:
You answered U1 to U4 on 2026-11-03. The answers are D1 to D5.

D1 (U1): (a) "Contract first, 2 adapters".

D2 (U2): "Install/use Playwright when required for accurate UI capture." Installing is allowed only when a capture needs it, and each install is recorded.

D3 (U3): "Keep Cheflabels' design kit separate from task-specific reviews. Reuse actual approved components and capture real screenshots." Any Cheflabels app change still goes through its own task.

D4 (U4): "Only explicitly approved components are approved" and "everything else remains candidate/unverified."

D5 (general): "Keep the solution framework-agnostic (Angular, React, Vue, etc.). Never invent application UI when real components or screenshots are available."

sections.title: Risks and assumptions
sections.text:
The Cheflabels kit page still loads translations over HTTP, and its development environment points at the live backend. A capture without an offline configuration contacts production, so that preview stays blocked until a separate Cheflabels task makes it offline.

Other risks are committed tokens in environment files, personal data in captures, running project code to capture, and fidelity limits. Examples of fidelity limits are the 500 px minimum width, fonts, Ionic md and iOS modes, and WebView differences.

Some screens cannot be captured without a server or device. They keep sketches and block visual approval.
sections.locator: FINDINGS.md E13, E16, E19; PLAN.md ## Agreement

sections.title: How it will be checked
sections.text:
Each ticket has a Verify line in TODO. U-T1 uses unit tests with fixture manifests and the package suite. U-T2 uses matching and drifted sources. U-T3 uses a fake browser. U-T4 uses fingerprint tests. U-T5 uses snapshot tests and a browser look at desktop and narrow width.

U-T6 and U-T7 capture with the network blocked. U-T7 also records fidelity limits. U-T8 makes one plan report per project with real previews, or "visual approval blocked" with the reason. Every capture is looked at for personal data before it goes into a report.
